To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
exogenous PLCz can be used to induce activation in bovine SCNT embryos and that this method of activation can support normal development and reprogramming of the genome.

the activation of bovine SCNT embryos with PLCZ cRNA can be used to produce high-quality embryos that have a gene expression and histone methylation pattern comparable with those observed in IVF embryos.

exogenous PLCz can be used to induce Ca(2) oscillations and to activate bovine somatic nuclear transfer embryos, and that activation by PLCz supports high rates of blastulation, but not the expression of some key genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach to activate bovine nuclear transfer (NT) derived embryos using the sperm-specific phospholipoase PLCZ.
the development of a method to improve the production of cloned animals and to increase our understanding of the mechanisms of nuclear reprogramming.
the development of a novel method for activating nuclear transfer embryos that may be used to improve the efficiency of this technique.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
activation of bovin SCNT embryos by PLCZ does not enhance the efficiency of nuclear reprogramming.
PLCZ can be utilized to activate bovine nuclear transfer-derived embryos, which is an important first step in the process of nuclear reprogramming.
the use of a fertilization-like response to activate nuclear transfer embryos improves some aspects of reprogramming but that further research is necessary to determine the mechanisms involved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of exogenous PLCz can improve nuclear reprogramming and that the use of a fertilization-like response may be a better approach than the use of combined chemical treatments to achieve nuclear transfer activation in cattle.
activation of nuclear transfer embryos by a sperm-specific phosphatase (PLCzeta) improves the efficiency of the process.

PLCZ cRNA can be used to artificially activate bovine nuclear transfer-derived embryos and supports the hypothesis that a more fertilization-like activation process can improve some aspects of nuclear programming.
The main takeaway from our work is that

activation by PLCz cRNA injection can support development of nuclear transfer embryos to the blastocyst stage and is associated with a similar gene expression profile compared to in vitro fertilized embryos, and that the use of DMAP/cycloheximide for activation of bovine SCNT embryos may not support optimal levels of histone methylation at the blastocyst.
the PLCZ can be injected into the ooplasm of bovine SCNT embryos and that this treatment is sufficient to induce activation and support blastocyst development.
activation of bovines SCNT embryos using PLCZ can be achieved with high blastocyst rates and gene expression profiles similar to that of embryos produced by in vitro fertilization.
